chunks: A storm may overtake you, and there may be none to prick you (for reforms).
Shall I be witness to my becoming heretic after acceptance of Faith and fighting in the company of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)?
"In that case I shall be misguided and I shall not be on the right path."
So you should return to your evil places, and get back on the traces of your heels.
Beware! Certainly you will meet, after me, overwhelming disgrace and sharp sword and tradition that will be adopted by the oppressors as a norm towards you.

key_terms.آبرٌ: one who pricks; a person who gives a gentle nudge or correction for reform
key_terms.حَاصِبٌ: storm or hail; a metaphor for a sudden calamity or event
key_terms.سُنَّةً: a tradition or norm adopted as a practice

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali predict about the fate of the Kharijites?
ai.summary: In this poignant address to the Kharijites, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts their hasty apostasy with his own steadfast faith and jihad alongside the Prophet, invoking the Quranic verse from Surah Az-Zumar to highlight their deviation. He foretells their ultimate humiliation and the establishment of a lasting tradition of oppression by tyrants, a prophecy historically fulfilled during the Umayyad era. This passage underscores the Shia view of the Kharijites as early exemplars of rigid extremism that paved the way for political tyranny.
